extracted.intended_audience: NIH/Fellowship reviewers, aging researchers, and grant applicants (F99/K00; gerontology/mental_health/cognitive_health researchers)
extracted.subtask_description: A predoctoral (F99) and postdoctoral (K00) mixed-methods research proposal investigating how physical and social living environments and ICT use affect social isolation and cognitive health in older adults, using NHATS longitudinal data and the I-CONECT randomized trial.

rubrics_metrics.name: Specific Aims (F99 & K00)
rubrics_metrics.description: Aim 1 (F99): examine the effect of physical and social environments on social isolation and cognitive health using a mixed-methods approach; ICT use is hypothesized to moderate these effects. Aim 2 (K00): examine the effectiveness of an ICT-enhanced conversational intervention on social isolation and cognitive health and explore co-designing a community-based, technology-facilitated intervention from an ETA perspective.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Specific Aims should be clearly stated and phase-specific (predoctoral vs postdoctoral), with explicit hypotheses about moderation/mediation and a plan to translate findings into an intervention design.

rubrics_metrics.name: H1: Physical environment → social isolation
rubrics_metrics.description: H1: Negative physical characteristics of the environment (community and home disorder) predict increased social isolation in the community.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Operationalize ‘negative physical characteristics’ using observer-rated community and home disorder measures and test longitudinal associations.

rubrics_metrics.name: H2: Social environment protective of isolation
rubrics_metrics.description: H2: Positive social environment factors (e.g., trust neighbors, people helping each other) are associated with less social isolation longitudinally.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Measure perceived social environment via respondent reports (sense of community/trust/helping) and model longitudinal effects.

rubrics_metrics.name: H3: Social environment mediates physical → isolation
rubrics_metrics.description: H3: Social environmental factors mediate the longitudinal association between physical environmental factors and social isolation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use mediation-capable longitudinal models (e.g., LGCM/SEM) to test whether social environment explains the pathway from physical disorder to isolation.

rubrics_metrics.name: H4: Physical environment → cognitive decline
rubrics_metrics.description: H4: Negative physical environments (disorder in community and homes) are longitudinally positively associated with deterioration in cognitive function.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Model cognitive trajectories as outcomes of physical environment indices controlling for covariates; use longitudinal data.

rubrics_metrics.name: H5: Social environment → cognitive decline
rubrics_metrics.description: H5: Positive social environment (neighborhood cohesion) is longitudinally associated with cognitive function.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assess neighborhood cohesion and test its association with cognitive outcomes over time.

rubrics_metrics.name: H6: Social isolation mediates environment → cognition
rubrics_metrics.description: H6: Social isolation mediates the longitudinal association between physical and social environments and cognitive function.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Test mediation paths in longitudinal SEM/LGCM frameworks to evaluate indirect effects through social isolation.

rubrics_metrics.name: H7: ICT use moderates environment → isolation
rubrics_metrics.description: H7: ICT use will moderate the longitudinal association between physical and social environments and social isolation; specifically, social-purpose ICT users are less likely to be socially isolated.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Treat instrumental, social, and medical ICT use as independent moderators and test interaction effects in longitudinal models.

rubrics_metrics.name: Significance (gap and impact)
rubrics_metrics.description: Demonstrate the public health significance of social isolation and cognitive decline among older adults, identify the gap (limited longitudinal evidence on environment effects and role of ICT), and explain how proposed work will build evidence and inform interventions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Frame research within Ecological Theory of Aging (ETA), cite epidemiologic and economic burden, and argue contribution to theory and intervention design.

rubrics_metrics.name: Dataset: NHATS waves 5-8
rubrics_metrics.description: Use NHATS waves 5 (2015) to 8 (2018), a stratified three-stage sample of Medicare beneficiaries aged 65+, with sample replenishment at wave 5 and 8,334 complete cases in wave 5.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Justify wave selection (availability of physical environment measures, replenishment), account for sampling design (PSUs, SSUs), and apply sampling weights for representativeness.

rubrics_metrics.name: Measurement: Physical environment (interviewer observation)
rubrics_metrics.description: Interviewer-rated measures standing in front of home: community items (litter, graffiti, vacant buildings) on 4-point scale; home/building condition dichotomous items (broken windows, crumbling foundation, missing bricks, roof problems, uneven walking surface, continuous sidewalks reverse coded); inside home items (peeling paint, pests, broken furniture, flooring repair need, tripping hazards, clutter). Sum scores derived for community, home/building, and inside home.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prefer interviewer observation over census-by-zip measures for accuracy; derive scale scores by summing items; reverse-code where needed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Measurement: Social environment (respondent report)
rubrics_metrics.description: Three items: whether people in the community know each other very well, are willing to help each other, and can be trusted; measured on 3-point scale (1=agree a lot, 2=agree a little, 3=do not agree) and summed into a social environment score.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use summed score as social cohesion index; ensure consistent coding direction for interpretation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Measurement: ICT use (three types)
rubrics_metrics.description: NHATS assesses instrumental internet use (shop online, pay bills/banking), social internet use (visited social network sites in last month), and internet use for medical purposes (order/refill prescriptions, contact providers, handle insurance, get health info). The three aspects are treated as independent moderators.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Model each ICT type separately as moderators of environment effects; consider differential effects by purpose.

rubrics_metrics.name: Measurement: Social isolation (6-item index & thresholds)
rubrics_metrics.description: Constructed from six dichotomous indicators: no marriage/partnership; no family to talk with about important things; no friend to talk with about important things; never meeting family/friends in past month; no participation in religious service; no participation in club/class/organization. Sum score ranges 0–6; <1 = least isolated, 2–3 = somewhat isolated, ≥4 = socially isolated.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Code higher scores = more isolation; use thresholding as descriptive categories and continuous score for modeling.

rubrics_metrics.name: Measurement: Cognitive health
rubrics_metrics.description: For self-respondents: memory via immediate & delayed word recall; orientation via date/month/year/day and naming President & Vice President; executive function via clock drawing test. For proxy interviews use AD-8 Dementia Screening (memory, temporal orientation, judgment, function).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use these objective/structured tasks to construct cognitive outcome measures; use proxy AD-8 when necessary and account for mode differences.

rubrics_metrics.name: Control variables (covariates)
rubrics_metrics.description: Include demographics reported as predictors of social isolation: age, gender, race, education level, marital status, income, and self-rated health.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include these as standard covariates in longitudinal models to account for confounding.

rubrics_metrics.name: Quantitative data management and pre-model checks
rubrics_metrics.description: Data management and recoding with Stata 15 SE; run univariate analysis and correlations to estimate effect sizes and detect multicollinearity prior to model building.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Perform descriptive and diagnostic checks (collinearity, distributions) before fitting longitudinal models; document coding and transformations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Quantitative analysis: Latent Growth Curve Modeling (LGCM) & software
rubrics_metrics.description: Use LGCM (a special case of SEM) to model longitudinal relationships, mediation paths, and moderation; models run in Mplus 8. Handle missing data with Full Information Maximum Likelihood (FIML). Apply sampling weights.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Choose LGCM/SEM when testing mediation/moderation over time; use FIML for missingness and incorporate sampling design weights.

rubrics_metrics.name: Model fit criteria (RMSEA, CFI, TLI thresholds)
rubrics_metrics.description: Evaluate model fit using RMSEA, CFI, and TLI: RMSEA < 0.05, CFI and TLI > 0.90 considered acceptable; CFI and TLI > 0.95 indicate good model fit.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Report fit indices and interpret against these thresholds; consider model modification only with theoretical justification.

rubrics_metrics.name: Handling missing data and estimation
rubrics_metrics.description: Use Full Information Maximum Likelihood (FIML) estimation to handle missing data in SEM/LGCM models.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Implement FIML in Mplus and report assumptions about missingness; consider sensitivity analyses if appropriate.

rubrics_metrics.name: Qualitative design: purposive sampling & focus groups
rubrics_metrics.description: Recruit focus group participants purposefully among completed I-CONECT participants using maximum variation sampling to get diverse living environment conditions; two focus groups at each of two sites (OHSU & UM), one for intervention and one for control; target 8 participants per group (total N=32); only invite participants who have completed I-CONECT to avoid contamination.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use purposeful sampling to capture diverse experiences; separate groups by intervention status; justify sample size and site selection.

rubrics_metrics.name: Qualitative data collection: instrument development
rubrics_metrics.description: Develop interview guide informed by ETA and in consultation with qualitative/mixed-methods experts and I-CONECT staff; PD/PI facilitates focus groups.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ground interview questions in theory (ETA) and pilot/consult with experts for content validity.

rubrics_metrics.name: Qualitative data analysis: inductive coding and reliability
rubrics_metrics.description: Audio-record and transcribe verbatim; analyze transcripts using inductive content analysis with at least two trained independent coders using Nvivo 12; coders meet regularly to discuss coding framework and reconcile differences; use Cohen’s kappa as indicator for inter-rater reliability.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Document coding procedures, calculate and report inter-rater reliability (Cohen's kappa), and iteratively refine coding schema.

rubrics_metrics.name: Mixed-methods integration strategy
rubrics_metrics.description: Concurrent quantitative and qualitative inquiries; use qualitative data to explain quantitative findings and elicit participant insights for designing a sustainable environmental-focused technology program; findings from both components will inform intervention development.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Plan for joint interpretation of results, specify how qualitative themes will contextualize statistical findings, and use integrated evidence to guide intervention co-design.

rubrics_metrics.name: I-CONECT RCT design and sample
rubrics_metrics.description: I-CONECT: randomized controlled trial conducted at OHSU and UM; recruit 160 socially isolated adults aged 75+ per site and randomize to video-chat intervention vs control (as of Oct 2019, 105 subjects participating).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Describe eligibility (age, social isolation), randomization, intervention modality (internet-facilitated conversational engagement via video-chat), and planned use of trial data for K00 analyses.

rubrics_metrics.name: Justification for measurement choices
rubrics_metrics.description: Interviewer observations are preferred to census-by-zip code measures because they provide more accurate information about the physical environment complexity of participants.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide rationale for measurement selection and discuss implications for measurement error and ecological validity.

rubrics_metrics.name: Sampling and response-rate transparency
rubrics_metrics.description: Report NHATS response rates and sampling details: overall response rate at wave 5 was 76% (96% continuing sample, 63% newly enrolled); describe stratified three-stage sample design (95 PSUs, 655 zip codes SSUs) and oversampling strategies.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide transparency on representativeness and potential biases; apply sampling weights in analysis to account for design and oversampling.
